source.title: Boss: “Clock out exactly at 5:00 or you’re written up. No exceptions.”   So I did
source.text:
My old office had a strict “no overtime without pre-approval” policy. Fair enough. But my boss was the type who would dump last-minute work on you at 4:50 and then act shocked when you stayed late.

One Friday he hands me a stack of client files at 4:47 and says, “I need these reviewed and the summary email sent before you leave.”

I look at the clock. “It’s 4:47. Policy says I have to be clocked out by 5:00 or I get written up.”

He waves it off. “Just finish it. Don’t be difficult.”

I smile and say, “Of course.”

I open the first file, start reading… very… slowly. At 4:59 I save my progress, close the documents, and stand up.

Boss: “Where are you going? You’re not done.”

Me: “It’s 5:00. Policy is clear. Clock out exactly at 5:00 or written up. No exceptions.”

I clock out, grab my bag, and walk out while he’s still standing there with his mouth open.

Monday morning he calls me into his office, red-faced. “You left those files unfinished on purpose.”

Me: “I followed the rule you enforce every single day. Would you like me to write myself up for the overtime I didn’t do?”

He never gave me another last-minute dump after that. The files somehow got finished by someone else over the weekend.

Sometimes the best way to win is to follow the rules harder than they ever wanted.

notes: The boss's own no-overtime rule is the trap; button is that the files still got done, by someone else, on the weekend.
